Capital One. What's in your wallet?
Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Microsoft says a new fix is showing progress as a massive outage continues to disrupt email and workplace services.
The disruption began on Thursday and has impacted businesses, schools and government agencies around the world.
Anna Marie Yanny of member station KNKX in Seattle reports.
Outlook emails, Microsoft Teams messaging and other 365 services were affected.
Gary Renville runs the nonprofit Project Access Northwest.
His small team connects low income patients with health and dental care.
We actually had to shut down our business because of the outage. I had to send my employees home.
He says without Teams and Outlook, they didn't have a secure way to talk to patients.
Microsoft spent much of the day working on the outage, saying they were pursuing "all available pathways to restore service."
For NPR News, I'm Anna Marie Yanny in Seattle.
Microsoft is a financial supporter of NPR.
Tech company NVIDIA is searching for a new leader following the resignation of Jensen Huang.
The co-founder stepped down amid allegations on multiple affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China.
NPR's John Ruich reports the company is turning to a familiar face while the board searches for a permanent replacement.
The board said the company's CFO, Collette Kress, is stepping into the role while they search for a permanent replacement for Huang.
Kress is a longtime NVIDIA executive. She joined NVIDIA 13 years ago after working in finance at tech companies for many years before that.
Jensen Huang was very much the public face of the company, but Kress has been prominent.
She has, for instance, spent on dozens of earnings calls alongside Huang when the company reports its quarterly results.
So she's a known quantity inside NVIDIA with its investors and with companies it does business with.
That's NPR's John Ruich reporting.
U.S. envoy Steve Wickhoff and Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday.
The meeting followed talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Speaking on the airport tarmac, Kushner said Europe would henceforth take part in the talks.
We cannot conclude this deal that the Europeans being at the table, we've been telling President Putin that we believe that's very important.
But Putin has backed off none of his hard-line positions and said any peacekeeping force in Ukraine would be a legitimate target.
Zelensky spoke earlier about the star-shield satellite connection being slowed down again.
He called it vital to intercepting Russia's new jet-powered drones.
Because of the speed restrictions, we simply cannot catch up with them in time.
And this means more Russian strikes get through and more of our civilians are killed.
Ukraine is participating in the talks but does not believe Putin wants to stop the war.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
This is NPR News.
The 27th annual Latin Grammys were held in Las Vegas last night.
NPR's Felix Contreras reports it was a big night for Latin folk music and was highlighted by a surprise guest presenter.
Twenty-year-old Argentine vocalist Milo Hota won Latin Grammys in three different music categories for his album of Argentine folk music, La Vida Eramar Escorte.
Spanish vocalist Rosalia's genre-defying album Lux won the top spots of Album of the Year as well as Song of the Year and Best Pop Song.
Recitone pioneer Daddy Yankee was recognized as the Latin Recording Academy's Person of the Year, which was presented by an unannounced appearance by R&B icon Janet Jackson.
And the newly minted congressman-elect from the Texas 15th congressional district, Bobby Polido, picked up his third Latin Grammy this year for Best Tejano album, Felix Contreras, NPR News.
A Democratic political group is launching an effort to address voters' concerns about artificial intelligence ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
The organization is planning to spend more than a million dollars studying public views on AI and how Democrats should talk about it.
The announcement coincides with a gathering of party leaders in Denver to celebrate their midterm wins and plan what comes next.
President Trump is pushing for rapid AI development. Some Democrats are calling for tighter rules or to slow down development.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.
